notes: Term-request re-check (#12): this was recorded as an ENVO term request on the premise that "ENVO has only plant-associated and animal-associated environment with no shared parent". Its definition, 'an environmental system which is determined by a living organism', is exactly what this top-level bin means: an isolate whose habitat is a living host. Grounded EXACT. The claim was made by hand and never machine-rechecked, which is the same staleness the class-level sweeps have a gate for and individually-decided records did not.

object_label: environment associated with a plant part or small plant
notes: Cohort review: 'Root-Rhizome' is root OR rhizome; PO:0004542 'rhizome' silently drops the root, which is the commoner isolation site of the two. Kept as a narrower kind of the plant-part environment rather than grounded to half of itself.

Term-request re-check (#12): 'Decomposing-plant' was left ungrounded after NCIT:C14258 'Plant' was refused for naming the organism rather than the decomposing material. That refusal was right; the conclusion that no term fits was not. ENVO:01000628 'plant litter' is dead plant material — leaves, bark, needles, twigs — which is what the bin holds. CLOSE rather than EXACT because ENVO's definition adds 'that has fallen to the ground', and standing dead plant material is decomposing plant that is not litter.

Cohort review: NCIT:C17649 'Other' is a bucket with no meaning of its own, and it absorbs 'Rodentia-Other' too — one record labelled 'Other' holding rodents and invertebrates. The invertebrate-associated environment terms in the slice are all aquatic-qualified. Real habitat, no term.

Residual-host review (#192): BacDive's live vocabulary places `Rodentia (Other)` under `#Host` as the sibling of `#Muridae (Mouse/Rat)`. It is a real animal-host environment, not NCIT:C17649 `Other`; that contentless lexical target remains rejected. ENVO:01001002 is genuinely broader and the category is HOST_ASSOCIATED. The source bucket means rodent hosts not assigned to the Muridae sibling, so it stays minted and separate: merging would erase the family-rank boundary, while requesting an ontology class defined by a mutable “everything else” exclusion would make its meaning change whenever BacDive adds a sibling. Hamsters and voles remain in scope despite vernacular mouse names; the attesting Actinobacillus capsulatus includes a reported rabbit-derived type strain outside Rodentia, so source assignment is preserved as evidence rather than treated as a taxonomic guarantee.

Host-taxon reversal (#114): this was NOT_APPLICABLE on the reasoning that 'a host taxon is not a habitat'. That reasoning is wrong, and the corpus already contradicted it — the same kind of concept was treated as a habitat for Sponge, Nematoda, Reptilia, Mammals, Birds and Fish, which keep their own identity and a term request for an <X>-associated environment. Host-associated > Porifera was NOT_APPLICABLE while its own child Porifera > Sponge was a term request.An organism acting as a host IS a habitat: it is where the microbe lives, and ENVO models exactly this at plant-associated, animal-associated and fungi-associated environment. What is not a habitat is the TAXON TERM — a phylum is a class of organisms, not a place — so the taxon stays an xref (#99) and the concept keeps its own identity as a term-request candidate. NOT_APPLICABLE said the concept is not a habitat, which is a stronger and false claim. Category set to HOST_ASSOCIATED (#200): the row already claims ENVO:01001002 'animal-associated environment' as the nearest broader term, which is the claim that a living animal host defines the habitat, and every other record carrying that parent is HOST_ASSOCIATED. The category column was left blank here, so the seeder's default stood and five domestic-mammal hosts stayed in OTHER while their siblings did not. The reasoning above is unchanged.

Cohort review: NCIT:C43963 'Creek' drops the river half. ENVO:00000029 'watercourse' is the genus of both river and creek, so it covers the source instead of picking one branch of it. Merges with the existing PREGO watercourse record, which is the harmonization working.

Cohort review: flagged by the screen as a dropped modifier, but the dropped word is a second word for the same thing rather than a lost qualifier — 'plant' and 'factory' are both the industrial sense here, not vegetation, so ENVO:01000536 'factory' loses nothing. Read from the label alone: neither this repo nor kg-microbe carries a BacDive category path to check the reading against (#51).

object_label: environment associated with a plant part or small plant
notes: Cohort review: NCIT:C45313 'Part' is a bucket term carrying none of the meaning. A surface-sterilized plant part is the endophyte isolation route and is a narrower kind of plant-part environment.

Adversarial review of #120 (#123): #114 correctly reversed this from NOT_APPLICABLE — a cnidarian host is a habitat — but overshot by making it a term-request candidate. The term already exists: ENVO:01001179 'cnidarian-associated environment', 'an environmental system determined by a cnidarian or part of a cnidarian', present in the vendored slice with that exact label. Requesting it would have been requesting a duplicate. Grounded EXACT. Note that GROUND does not carry an xref the way NOT_APPLICABLE and CONFIRM_UNGROUNDED do, so the taxon link (mesh:D003063 / mesh:D037421) is not retained on the record; the upstream mapping remains in data/raw/. Risky-grounding review (#12): the seeder grounded 'Host-associated > Annelida > Gills' to UBERON:0011150 'pharyngeal arch derived gill'. Annelid gills are not pharyngeal-arch derived — that term is vertebrate-specific, and annelids have no pharyngeal arches — so the identity was an anatomical error the label match could not see. ITEM reassessment #1332: this source is the anterior chamber of a crustacean hindgut, not the eye chamber UBERON:0001766. BTO:0000510 explicitly denotes vertebrate embryonic hindgut and cannot subsume it. Bogataj et al. distinguish anterior chamber and papillate region in Porcellio scaber (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30564048/ DOI:10.3897/zookeys.801.22395). Retain the minted regional habitat UNGROUNDED because no fitting identity or strictly broader regional term was verified; whole UBERON:0001046 hindgut is not a compartment superclass. The independent GOLD whole-hindgut context parent is excluded under #1331. Preserve node 7325 and the full source path; no universal crustacean microbiome or sample identity is inferred. This supersedes the 2026-08-16 GROUND_AS_PARENT decision, retained in Git and append-only session history.

Risky-grounding review (#12): the seeder grounded 'Birds > Digestive system > Crop > Lumen' to UBERON:0000464 'anatomical space' as its identity. The committed sourdough report kept this as a real habitat with no defensible identity term: FOODON:03302481 'sourdough bread' is the baked product after the microbial habitat has ended, and the unvendored FoodOn sourdough-starter classes are commodity or facet-bundle terms that over-claim relative to GOLD's Engineered > Food production > Sourdough source. ENVO:03600040 'fermentation starter' is a true broader parent because sourdough is a maintained flour-water starter used to acidify and leaven bread dough. Path: Engineered > Food production > Sourdough

Source-identity correction (#2051): BacDive Egg is a host-body-product isolation category, not a food-only vocabulary branch. Both explicitly carry Host Body Product > Urogenital tract > Egg. Reject FOODON:00001274 'egg food product' and its vertebrate-food restriction; retain the native source habitat with HOST_ASSOCIATED coarse placement, not whole-organism ontology identity or NOT_APPLICABLE. No verified exact identity for this source scope is established in the committed slice; this is not global ontology absence. Preserve all 35 STRAIN-unit source assertions and all 25 displayed taxon observations/ranks from the 30-taxon pool. Two exact-strain witnesses do not reconstruct every original member or justify a source split, characteristic-presence claim or merger with GOLD Egg products.

Risky-grounding review (#12): the seeder made ENVO:00002204 'anthropogenic contamination feature' the identity of BacDive's 'Contamination' category — the highest-volume risky grounding at 474 strains. The term asserts two things BacDive does not: that the contamination is anthropogenic, and that the thing is a geographic feature with elevated contaminants in its materials. BacDive's category says only that a strain was isolated as a contaminant, which is as often of a product, a culture or a cleanroom as of a place. These are different concepts rather than a broader and a narrower one, so the term is not a parent either — parent_habitats asserts the parent is BROADER. Kept as an xref (#99), which records that upstream saw a connection without this repo asserting one.

Non-habitat screen (#12): 'Host-associated > Algae' was grounded EXACT to FOODON:03411301 'algae', which FOODON defines as 'an informal term for a large, diverse group of photosynthetic eukaryotic ORGANISMS'. An organism is not a habitat, and because the seeder derives a GOLD child's parent from its path node, that identity also became the parent_habitats entry of 14 records under Host-associated > Algae — publishing 'is-a algae the organism group' as a broader-habitat claim 14 times over. The existing organism-identity screen could not see it: it tests ancestry against NCIT and mesh roots, and FOODON files both the organism and the material under one 'organism material' root, so there is no structural signal to test. The concept itself is real — algae as host — and is the same family as the sponge, nematode and reptile requests, so it becomes a term request with the FOODON term kept as an xref (#99) rather than an identity.
